```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` + managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`). The overlay enforces our managed tables on every `chezmoi apply` while preserving whatever herdr writes back at runtime (see [Config management](#config-management-why-modify_)).
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
23	
24	### Named sessions
25	
26	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
27	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
28	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
29	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
30	
31	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
32	
33	## cwd & workspace-naming model
34	
35	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
36	
37	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
38	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
39	- **New tabs spawn at the workspace root, not the focused pane's cwd.** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *split* inherits the focused pane's cwd, but a *new tab* falls back to the workspace's cwd (often `$HOME`). Confirmed: every non-first tab's root pane has `cwd = $HOME`.
40	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
41	
42	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
43	
44	| value | meaning |
45	|---|---|
46	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane/workspace (split → focused pane's live cwd; new tab → workspace root) |
47	| `home` | `$HOME` |
48	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
49	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
50	
51	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab in the focused pane's live cwd** — only an explicit `herdr tab create --cwd …` does (verified: `tab create --cwd PATH` spawns the new tab's shell in `PATH`). For a "new tab here" key, bind a command pane to `herdr tab create --cwd "$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD" --focus` (e.g. on `prefix+C`; native `prefix+c` stays = workspace root):
52	
53	```toml
54	[[keys.command]]
55	key = "prefix+C"
56	type = "pane"
57	command = "herdr tab create --cwd \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD\" --focus"
58	description = "new tab in the current pane's cwd"
59	```
60	
61	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
62	
63	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
66	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
67	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
68	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
69	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
70	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
71	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
72	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
73	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
74	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
75	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | **No format-string interpolation** | **Gap** — native agent dots replace the agent part |
76	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
77	
78	## Keybindings
79	
80	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
81	
82	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
83	
84	| Key | Action | Type |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
87	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
88	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
89	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
90	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
91	| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
92	| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
93	
94	> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
95	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
96	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
97	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
98	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
99	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
100	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
101	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
102	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
103	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
104	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
105	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
106	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
107	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
108	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
109	
110	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
111	
112	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot`)
113	
114	Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
115	
116	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
119	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
120	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
121	| `hhere [CMD...]` | `<basename $PWD>` | single tab, plain shell at `$PWD` (or `-p DIR`); optional `CMD` in the root pane |
122	| `hroot [CMD...]` | `<basename git-root>` | same as `hhere` but at the current git root (falls back to `$PWD`) |
123	
124	- **The plain-open pair (`hhere` / `hroot`)** fills the gap where every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent layout. With tmux, `tmux new-session` lands you in `$PWD` directly; herdr adds a Workspace layer, so without these you'd launch herdr, create a space (which opens at `$HOME` per `new_cwd`), then `cd` by hand. `hhere` does the one-shot: `herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → attach if outside. No git requirement; the optional command runs **raw** (no specstory/on-exit wrapping — that stays with `hcode`/`hvibe`). `hhere -h` / `hroot -h` for flags. **Label caveat**: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to its root pane's *live* cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see the **cwd & workspace-naming model** section above), so the idempotent-focus is best-effort — a drifted label makes a re-run open a fresh workspace.
125	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
126	- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
127	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
128	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
129	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
130	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
131	
132	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
133	
134	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
135	
136	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
137	
138	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
139	
140	```bash
141	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
142	```
143	
144	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
145	
146	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
147	
148	## Television integration
149	
150	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Two ship here:
151	
152	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
153	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
154	
155	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
156	
157	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
158	
159	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
160	
161	```bash
162	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
163	```
164	
165	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
166	
167	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
168	
169	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
170	
171	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
174	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
175	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
176	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
177	
178	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
179	
180	### Config management (why `modify_`)
181	
182	herdr can rewrite `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` at runtime — finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime.
183	
184	This file was originally seeded once with the `create_` prefix so `chezmoi apply` wouldn't clobber that writeback. The cost: **repo edits never reached an already-seeded machine** — split-key rebinds and comment fixes made in the source silently never arrived without a manual `cp … source-path` refresh. That is the real reason a host could feel "out of sync" while `chezmoi diff` showed clean (the diff was clean *because* `create_` never re-touches the file). Note this is independent of hosts: `chezmoi diff` of the source against each host's live file can be byte-identical yet a repo edit still won't land until you refresh.
185	
186	It is now a **`modify_` overlay** — `dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, a small script that:
187	
188	- uses the managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` as the base (comments + tmux-parity rationale), enforcing the `[theme]` / `[ui]` / `[terminal]` / `[keys]` tables on every apply, and
189	- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
190	
191	TOML has no `jq`, so the merge runs in Python via `uv run --with tomlkit` (tomlkit round-trips comments **and** the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables; stdlib `tomllib` is read-only and the codex `modify_` emitter can't emit AoT). It degrades to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw managed template, so a fresh host without Python still gets a full config. Second TOML-overlay precedent alongside `~/.codex/config.toml` (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`).
192	
193	To change herdr's managed config, edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` and `chezmoi apply` — it now reaches every host. Validate with `herdr server reload-config` (reports keybind collisions in its `diagnostics`; an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means the config — including array key bindings — parsed clean).
194	
195	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
196	
197	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
198	
199	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
200	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
201	
202	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
203	
204	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
205	
206	```bash
207	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
208	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
209	```
210	
211	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
212	
213	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
214	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
215	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
216	
217	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
218	
219	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
220	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
221	
222	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
223	
224	```bash
225	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
226	```
227	
228	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
229	
230	## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
231	
232	The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
233	
234	Three ways to resolve it, in order of preference here:
235	
236	1. **Double-prefix passthrough (recommended, zero config).** tmux keeps its default `bind -T prefix C-b send-prefix` (confirmed present in this repo — not overridden), so **`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b`** forwards a literal `Ctrl+b` to the inner herdr; its prefix bindings then work normally (`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b c` = inner new tab). No herdr or tmux change needed — classic tmux-in-tmux muscle memory.
237	2. **Rebind the inner herdr prefix.** Set `keys.prefix` (e.g. `"ctrl+a"` / `"ctrl+space"`) so the inner herdr uses a non-colliding prefix — one keystroke instead of the double-tap. Cost: it changes herdr's prefix even when run standalone (no longer matching tmux's `Ctrl+b`).
238	3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
239	
240	Notes: this repo's tmux uses many root-table `bind -n C-*` bindings that **shadow** inner-app `Ctrl` keys, so herdr's prefix-free *direct* terminal shortcuts aren't reliable under tmux — reach herdr actions through its prefix (via 1 or 2). herdr's own `allow_nested` (config, default `false`) governs herdr-inside-**herdr** only (detected via `HERDR_ENV`), not herdr-inside-tmux.
241	
242	## AI usage / quota status
243	
244	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into. A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
245	
246	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
247	
248	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
249	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
250	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
251	- **Per-key pane resize.** tmux binds `prefix+H/J/K/L` (and `M-hjkl` for fine steps) to resize directly; herdr has no per-key resize — it uses a modal `resize_mode` (`prefix+r`), then `h/j/k/l`. Not exact parity, but a close analog.
252	
253	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
254	
255	## See also
256	
257	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
258	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
259

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
5	# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
6	# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
7	# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
8	# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
9	# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
10	# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
11	#
12	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
13	# new contents on stdout.
14	#
15	# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
19	#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
22	#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
23	#
24	# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
25	# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
26	# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
27	# round-trips both.
28	#
29	# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
30	# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
31	# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
32	# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
33	#
34	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
35	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
36	# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
37	# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
38	# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
39	set -eu
40	
41	tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
42	trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM
43	
44	cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
45	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
46	TOML
47	
48	live=$(cat)
49	
50	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -
54	else
55	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
56	  cat "$tmpl_file"
57	  exit 0
58	fi
59	
60	HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63	
64	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
65	with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
66	    template_text = fh.read()
67	
68	
69	def emit_template():
70	    sys.stdout.write(template_text)
71	
72	
73	# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
74	try:
75	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
76	except ModuleNotFoundError:
77	    try:
78	        import tomli as tomllib
79	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
80	        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
81	        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
82	        emit_template()
83	        sys.exit(0)
84	
85	# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
86	# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
87	try:
88	    import tomlkit
89	except ModuleNotFoundError:
90	    print(
91	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
92	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
93	        file=sys.stderr,
94	    )
95	    emit_template()
96	    sys.exit(0)
97	
98	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
99	
100	live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
101	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
102	live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
103	
104	# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
105	for key, value in live.items():
106	    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
107	        continue
108	    doc[key] = value
109	
110	sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
111	PYEOF
112
```

4	#
5	# Toggle @bookmark_status on a tmux window. Invoked by the MouseDown3Status
6	# right-click menu in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl.
7	#
8	# Usage:
9	#   toggle-bookmark.sh <window-id> <glyph>
10	#     If @bookmark_status on <window-id> already equals <glyph>, unset it.
11	#     Otherwise overwrite it with <glyph>.
12	#
13	# Parallels workmux's @workmux_status — independent per-window user-option,
14	# both render side-by-side in the catppuccin window-text format
15	# (dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf lines 31–32). For CLI access use the
16	# generic API from dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh:
17	#   tmux_status_set bookmark '⭐'      # set on current window
18	#   tmux_status_clear bookmark         # clear on current window
19	#
20	# Why this script instead of inlining in display-menu: expressing
21	# "if current == X then unset else set to X" requires reading the option
22	# value first, and the quoting around emoji literals inside a nested tmux
23	# command list (display-menu → { run-shell … } → { set-option … }) is
24	# fragile. A tiny external script keeps the menu binding readable.
25	
26	set -eu
27	
28	win="${1:-}"
29	glyph="${2:-}"
30	
31	if [ -z "$win" ] || [ -z "$glyph" ]; then
32	    printf 'usage: %s <window-id> <glyph>\n' "$0" >&2
33	    exit 64
34	fi
35	
36	current=$(tmux show-options -wv -t "$win" '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || true)
37	
38	if [ "$current" = "$glyph" ]; then
39	    tmux set-option -w -t "$win" -u '@bookmark_status' 2>/dev/null || true
40	    tmux display-message "Bookmark cleared"
41	else
42	    tmux set-option -w -t "$win" '@bookmark_status' "$glyph"
43	    tmux display-message "Bookmark: $glyph"
44	fi
45

夠了,我把兩邊都摸清楚了,可以直接回答可行性。

## 短答:可以做,但不是走 tmux 那條路

你 tmux 的 `⭐/📌` 是靠 `@bookmark_status` user-option + status bar 的 `#{?@bookmark_status,…}` **format-string 內插**渲染的(`toggle-bookmark.sh` + `theme.catppuccin.conf:44-45`)。herdr **沒有 `#{@option}` 內插**,所以那個「自訂 glyph 塞進狀態列」的做法在 herdr 是真的 gap —— `docs/tools/herdr.md` 的 Gaps 也是這樣寫的。

但你要的其實不是「裝飾用書籤」,是**「agent 狀態 = done/idle,但任務我還沒 review」的 sticky 未讀旗標**。這個 herdr **有原生積木可以做**,而且剛好比 tmux 更貼合你的痛點。

## 關鍵積木:`pane report-metadata --custom-status`

```
herdr pane report-metadata <pane_id> --source ID \
    [--custom-status TEXT|--clear-custom-status] \
    [--state-label STATUS=TEXT|--clear-state-labels] [--ttl-ms N]
```

為什麼這個剛好解你的痛點 —— **它是一個獨立的 `--source`,跟 herdr 原生 agent 偵測分開**。你現在的痛點是:模型跑完 → `done` → 你點進去瞄一眼 → herdr 自動翻成 `idle` ✅ → mark 沒了。但如果未讀旗標是你自己用 `--source review` 推上去的,herdr 的原生偵測**不會去清它**,所以「點進去看一眼」不會弄丟旗標。這正是 tmux `@bookmark_status` 給你的那種「跟系統狀態正交、只有我手動能清」的語意。

(我剛查了你這台 live server,現在 14 個 agent 裡確實有 1 個 `done`、多個 `idle`、幾個 `working` —— `done` 和 `idle` 是分開的 state,但一 focus 就塌成 idle,所以你需要的正是一個不會被 focus 清掉的第二層旗標。)

## 建議的設計

**1. 兩個 shell helper**(放 `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`,跟 hvibe 那批一起):
- `hmark` → `herdr pane report-metadata "$HERDR_PANE_ID" --source review --custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"`(在 pane 內跑,吃 ambient `HERDR_PANE_ID`)
- `hunmark` → 同上 `--clear-custom-status`
- 也支援傳 pane id,這樣可以從別的 pane 標記某個 session

**2. Keybind** —— config 加一條 `[[keys.command]]`(例如 `prefix+m` toggle,`prefix+M` clear all)。

**3.(可選、但這才是真正解「容易忘記哪些未完成」)一個 `tv herdr-review` channel** —— 掃 `herdr pane list --json` 抓有 review 旗標的 pane,列成「未讀收件匣」,Enter → `herdr pane focus`(可選:focus 後自動清旗標,做成真正的 mark-read)。這比 tmux 版更強,因為 tmux 你的書籤只能在狀態列一格一格掃,這裡是一個可 fuzzy 的清單。跟現有的 `herdr-agent-panes.toml` 同一個模子。

## 需要先確認的兩個點(我沒動你的 live session)

1. **`--custom-status` 到底渲染在哪** —— 你已開 `show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders`,應該會出現在 pane border / sidebar label,但我不想在你 12 個真在跑的 agent 上亂推 metadata 去驗。
2. **不給 `--ttl-ms` 是否永久** —— 旗標是給 `ttl-ms` 加 TTL 的,理想上省略 = 永久;若不是,helper 就補一個很大的 TTL 或靠 shell hook 續命。

要的話我可以拿你其中一個 **idle** 的 pane 做一次**非破壞性**測試(推一個 `--source test-scratch` 的 label、看一眼渲染位置、馬上 `--clear`),確認上面兩點後再動手。

6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)

17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.

21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).

23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).

26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36	
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {

41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44	
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}

55	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
56	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
57	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
58	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
59	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
60	#
61	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
62	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
63	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
64	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
65	function _herdr_session_target() {
66	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
67	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
68	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
69	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
70	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
71	            | head -1)
72	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
73	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
74	            return 1
75	        fi
76	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
77	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
78	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
79	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
80	            return 1
81	        fi
82	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
83	        return 0
84	    fi
85	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
86	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
87	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
88	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then

91	            | head -1)
92	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"

95	    fi

100	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
101	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
102	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
103	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
104	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
105	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
106	    local session="${1:-default}"
107	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
108	        herdr
109	    else
110	        herdr session attach "$session"
111	    fi

305	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
306	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
307	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
308	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
309	
310	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
311	    local existing
312	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
313	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
314	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
315	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
316	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
317	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
318	        fi
319	        return 0
320	    fi
321	
322	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
323	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
324	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
325	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
326	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
327	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
328	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
329	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
330	        return 1
331	    fi
332	
333	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
334	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
335	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
336	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
337	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
338	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
339	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
340	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
341	        done
342	    else
343	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
344	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
345	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
346	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
347	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
348	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
349	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
350	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
351	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
352	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio
353	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
354	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
355	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
356	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
357	                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
358	            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
359	                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
360	                prev="$np"
361	            fi
362	            m=$((m+1))
363	        done
364	    fi
365	
366	    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
367	    local git_inner git_label
368	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
369	    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
370	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
371	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"
372	
373	    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
374	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
375	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
376	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
377	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
378	    fi
379	}
380	
381	# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
382	#
383	# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
384	#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
385	#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
386	# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
387	#
388	# Usage:
389	#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
390	#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
391	#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
392	#   hcode --no-specstory claude
393	#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
394	#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
395	function herdr-code() {
396	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
397	
398	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
399	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
400	        case "$1" in
401	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
402	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
403	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
404	            --session)      session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
405	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
406	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
407	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
408	            --agents)
409	                echo "hcode: --agents is hvibe-only (hcode is single-agent)." >&2
410	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2
411	                return 1 ;;
412	            -h|--help)
413	                cat <<'EOF'
414	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
415	
416	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
417	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
418	
419	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
420	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
421	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
422	Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
423	
424	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session;
425	run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses. --no-attach builds in the background.
426	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
427	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
428	
429	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
430	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
431	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
432	
433	--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart
434	
435	Examples:
436	  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
437	  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
438	  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
439	  hcode --on-exit kill claude
440	EOF
441	                return 0 ;;
442	            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
443	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
444	        esac
445	    done
446	
447	    case "$on_exit" in
448	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
449	        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
450	    esac
451	
452	    local repo_root
453	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
454	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
455	    else
456	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
457	    fi
458	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
459	        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
460	        return 1
461	    fi
462	
463	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
464	        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
465	        return 1
466	    fi
467	
468	    local repo label
469	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
470	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")
471	
472	    # Resolve target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
473	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
474	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
475	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
476	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
477	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
478	
479	    local existing
480	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
481	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
482	        echo "hcode: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
483	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
484	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
485	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
486	        fi
487	        return 0
488	    fi
489	
490	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
491	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
492	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
493	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
494	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
495	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
496	        echo "hcode: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
497	        return 1
498	    fi
499	
500	    # editor tab: nvim in the initial pane, agent split off to the right at ~25%.
501	    # --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane being split (nvim/left), so 0.75
502	    # leaves nvim at 75% and the new agent pane at 25%.
503	    herdr tab rename "$t0" editor >/dev/null 2>&1
504	    herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")" >/dev/null 2>&1
505	    local ap
506	    ap=$(herdr pane split "$p0" --direction right --ratio 0.75 --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
507	        | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
508	    [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane run "$ap" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
509	
510	    # monitor tab.
511	    local mon
512	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=btop
513	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=htop
514	    else                                       mon=top
515	    fi
516	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" monitor "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$mon" "$on_exit" "$mon")"
517	
518	    # Focus editor tab, nvim pane (left neighbor of the agent pane).
519	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
520	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
521	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
522	        [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane focus --direction left --pane "$ap" >/dev/null 2>&1
523	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
524	    fi
525	}
526	
527	# ── hhere: plain "open a workspace here + attach" ────────────────────────────
528	#
529	# herdr analog of `shere` (sesh-here). The lightweight counterpart to
530	# hvibe/hcode: create a herdr workspace at $PWD (or -p DIR), focus it, and
531	# attach a client when run from outside herdr. NO git requirement and NO agent
532	# layout — just a shell in the workspace root pane. This fills the gap where
533	# every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent pack; with
534	# tmux `tmux new-session` lands you in $PWD directly, but herdr adds a Workspace
535	# layer, so without this you'd launch herdr, create a space (opens at $HOME),
536	# then cd manually.
537	#
538	# Smart argument handling (mirrors shere):
539	#   hhere                          # plain shell at $PWD
540	#   hhere npm run dev              # bare args → run as the root-pane command
541	#   hhere -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
542	#   hhere -p ~/proj                # explicit path, plain shell
543	#   hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev    # explicit path + command
544	#
545	# The command (if any) runs raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping. That agent
546	# treatment stays with hcode/hvibe; hhere is deliberately lightweight.
547	#
548	# Idempotent per label (bare basename of the dir, matching herdr's own native
549	# auto-label convention). Caveat: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to the root
550	# pane's LIVE cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see docs/tools/herdr.md § cwd
551	# & workspace-naming), so the reuse is best-effort — if the label has drifted, a
552	# re-run creates a fresh workspace (arguably correct: you're elsewhere now).
553	#
554	# Usage:
555	#   hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
556	function herdr-here() {
557	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hhere: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
558	
559	    local cmd="" target="" no_attach=0 session_arg=""
560	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
561	        case "$1" in
562	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
563	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
564	            --session)    session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
565	            --no-attach)  no_attach=1; shift ;;
566	            -h|--help)
567	                cat <<'EOF'
568	hhere — open a plain herdr workspace here + attach (herdr analog of shere)
569	
570	Usage: hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
571	
572	Creates a herdr workspace at DIR (default $PWD), focuses it, and — when run
573	from OUTSIDE herdr — attaches a client so it is visible. No git repo required
574	and no agent layout: just a shell in the workspace root pane. For agent
575	layouts use hcode (single-agent) or hvibe (multi-agent).
576	
577	Smart argument handling:
578	  hhere                        # plain shell at $PWD
579	  hhere npm run dev            # bare args → run as the root-pane command
580	  hhere -c "npm run dev"       # explicit --command flag
581	  hhere -p ~/proj              # explicit path, plain shell
582	  hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev  # explicit path + command
583	
584	Idempotent: re-running in the same dir focuses the existing workspace.
585	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
586	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
587	--no-attach builds in the background.
588	EOF
589	                return 0 ;;
590	            -*)           echo "hhere: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
591	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
592	        esac
593	    done
594	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
595	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
596	
597	    local label
598	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
599	
600	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
601	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
602	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
603	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
604	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
605	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
606	
607	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
608	    local existing
609	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
610	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
611	        echo "hhere: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
612	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
613	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
614	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
615	        fi
616	        return 0
617	    fi
618	
619	    local ws_json ws p0
620	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$target" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
621	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
622	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
623	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ]; then
624	        echo "hhere: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
625	        return 1
626	    fi
627	
628	    # Optional command in the root pane (raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping).
629	    [ -n "$cmd" ] && herdr pane run "$p0" "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1
630	
631	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
632	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
633	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
634	    fi
635	}
636	
637	# ── hroot: like hhere but at the git-root ────────────────────────────────────
638	#
639	# herdr analog of `sroot` (sesh-root). Same as hhere except the target resolves
640	# to the current git top-level (falls back to $PWD outside a repo). Thin wrapper
641	# over herdr-here so there is one code path; -p is not accepted (the root IS the
642	# path), everything else (-c / bare command / --session / --no-attach) passes
643	# through.
644	#
645	# Usage:
646	#   hroot                          # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
647	#   hroot npm run dev              # + run a command
648	#   hroot -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
649	function herdr-root() {
650	    case "$1" in
651	        -h|--help)
652	            cat <<'EOF'
653	hroot — open a plain herdr workspace at the git-root + attach (analog of sroot)
654	
655	Usage: hroot [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
656	
657	Like hhere, but the workspace opens at the current git top-level (falls back to
658	$PWD outside a repo). All flags except --path pass through to hhere.
659	
660	  hroot                # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
661	  hroot npm run dev    # + run a command
662	EOF
663	            return 0 ;;
664	        -p|--path)
665	            echo "hroot: --path is not accepted (root is derived from git). Use hhere -p DIR." >&2
666	            return 1 ;;
667	    esac
668	    local root
669	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
670	    herdr-here -p "$root" "$@"
671	}
672	
673	# ── Aliases ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
674	alias hvibe='herdr-vibe'
675	alias hcode='herdr-code'
676	alias hhere='herdr-here'
677	alias hroot='herdr-root'
678
```

1	# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant

3	# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists

5	# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).

9	# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one

19	[metadata]

93	d='{split:\t:4}'
94	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
95	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
96	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
97	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
98	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
99	fi
100	'''
101	mode = "fork"
102
```

```text
1	# Session/workspace switcher cable channel for herdr (tv) — sesh analog
2	#
3	# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
4	# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches
5	# herdr WORKSPACES (the project-level unit) and opens new ones from zoxide
6	# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
7	# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
8	#
9	# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
10	#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
11	#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
12	#
13	# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.
14	
15	[metadata]
16	name = "herdr-sesh"
17	description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
18	requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]
19	
20	[source]
21	command = [
22	  '''herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]? | "ws\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.label)  (\(.pane_count)p, \(.tab_count)t)"' ''',
23	  '''zoxide query -l 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{print "dir",$0,$0}' ''',
24	]
25	display = "{split:\t:2}"
26	output = "{split:\t:1}"
27	
28	[preview]
29	command = '''
30	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
31	case "$kind" in
32	  ws)
33	    printf '\033[1mworkspace %s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
34	    herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq . 2>/dev/null \
35	      || herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null
36	    ;;
37	  dir)
38	    printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
39	    if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then eza -la --git --color=always "$ref" 2>/dev/null
40	    else ls -la "$ref" 2>/dev/null; fi
41	    ;;
42	esac
43	'''
44	
45	[ui]
46	input_header = "herdr Workspaces / Dirs"
47	
48	[keybindings]
49	enter = "actions:open"
50	ctrl-d = ["actions:close_ws", "reload_source"]
51	
52	[actions.open]
53	description = "Focus the workspace, or open a new workspace at the directory"
54	command = '''
55	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
56	[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0
57	case "$kind" in
58	  ws)  herdr workspace focus "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
59	  dir) herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
60	esac
61	'''
62	mode = "fork"
63	
64	[actions.close_ws]
65	description = "Close the selected herdr workspace"
66	command = '''
67	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
68	[ "$kind" = "ws" ] && [ -n "$ref" ] && herdr workspace close "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1
69	'''
70	mode = "fork"
71
```

2	#
3	# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
4	# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other (or

9	# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
10	# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves any keys herdr writes back at
11	# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [update] / [experimental]).
12	#

21	# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
22	# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
23	# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
24	# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.
25

27	name = "catppuccin"          # mocha (dark)

30	dark_name = "catppuccin"

34	pane_borders = true
35	pane_gaps = true
36	confirm_close = true
37	show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true
38	
39	[terminal]
40	shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
41	# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
42	#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
43	#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
44	# NOTE: a split's source is the focused pane (→ inherits its live cwd), but a
45	# NEW TAB's source is the WORKSPACE root, so new tabs open at the workspace cwd
46	# (often $HOME), NOT the focused pane's live cwd. No new_cwd value changes that;
47	# for "new tab here" use `herdr tab create --cwd …`. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
48	new_cwd = "follow"
49	
50	# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
51	# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
52	# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
53	# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
54	[keys]
55	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
56	split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
57	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
58	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
59	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)
60	
61	# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
62	# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
63	# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
64	# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
65	# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
66	# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
67	# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
68	# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
69	switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
70	focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)

73	# prefix+w opens the workspace navigator; navigate_workspace_* are the

44	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
45	
46	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
47	
48	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
49	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
50	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
51	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
52	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
53	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
54	
55	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.
