1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22	
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25	
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh
# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
# herdr's per-pane custom-status metadata (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source
# review --custom-status …`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
#
# Why custom-status and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. Verified: a
# pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so
# peeking into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
#
# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
# surfaces the `custom_status` field, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO
# --json flag) lets the `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No
# sidecar file.
#
# Usage:
#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
#
# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
# focus_clear action. Keep the marker MATCH substring ("REVIEW") in sync with
# that channel's jq filter (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml).
set -eu

SOURCE_ID='review'
MATCH='REVIEW'                 # substring the tv channel filters on (glyph-agnostic)
DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'

usage() {
    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 64
}

command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }

action="${1:-}"
pane="${2:-}"
status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"

[ -n "$action" ] || usage
[ -n "$pane" ] || usage

_set() {
    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --custom-status "$status" >/dev/null
    echo "review flag set on $pane"
}

_clear() {
    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --clear-custom-status >/dev/null
    echo "review flag cleared on $pane"
}

case "$action" in
    set)   _set ;;
    clear) _clear ;;
    toggle)
        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
            | jq -r '.result.pane.custom_status // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
        case "$current" in
            *"$MATCH"*) _clear ;;
            *)          _set ;;
        esac ;;
    *) usage ;;
esac

```

```toml
# Review-pending inbox cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware
#
# Lists herdr panes carrying a "review-pending" flag (⭐) — the ones whose agent
# finished but you haven't reviewed yet. Companion to `herdr-agent-panes.toml`;
# the flag is set by hmark / prefix+m (see dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh)
# and stored as the pane's `custom_status` metadata, orthogonal to agent state.
# Bound to `prefix+i` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB but KEEPS the ⭐ (you may still be
# mid-review). Alt+C = focus AND clear the flag ("mark read"). herdr has no
# "focus pane by id" (pane focus is directional only), so we focus at tab
# granularity — enough with one agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) via jq,
# filtered to panes whose custom_status contains "REVIEW" (glyph-agnostic; keep
# in sync with the MATCH substring in review-mark.sh):
#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
#   3. custom_status  (⭐ REVIEW)
#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)

[metadata]
name = "herdr-review"
description = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐) — jump to sessions you flagged for later"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | select(.custom_status? // "" | test("REVIEW")) | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.custom_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:3}  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'
printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
'''

[ui]
input_header = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐)"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:focus"
alt-t = "actions:focus"
alt-c = ["actions:focus_clear", "reload_source"]
ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"

[actions.focus]
description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab (keep the ⭐)"
command = '''
ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.focus_clear]
description = "Jump to the pane AND clear the ⭐ (mark read)"
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'; ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$pane" ] && "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh" clear "$pane" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_id]
description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy

else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''

[actions.copy_dir]
description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:4}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"

245	## AI usage / quota status
246	
247	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into. A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
248	
249	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
250	
251	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
252	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
253	- **Status-bar format glyphs + bookmarks** (⭐/📌/🔖): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation. Native agent dots cover the agent part; manual bookmarks have no analog.
254	- **Per-key pane resize.** tmux binds `prefix+H/J/K/L` (and `M-hjkl` for fine steps) to resize directly; herdr has no per-key resize — it uses a modal `resize_mode` (`prefix+r`), then `h/j/k/l`. Not exact parity, but a close analog.
255	
256	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
257	
258	## See also
259	
260	- [tmux setup](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)
261	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
262
```

```text
40:herdr 追蹤 cwd 的方式跟 tmux 不同,會顛覆兩個常見預期（皆用 `herdr pane list` 驗證）:
42:- **每個 pane 有兩個 cwd。** `cwd` = shell 的*啟動*目錄（spawn 時固定）;`foreground_cwd` = *即時* cwd,透過 **OSC 7** shell 整合追蹤。shell 裡 `cd` 會更新 `foreground_cwd`;啟動 `cwd` 永不變。
80:| 每視窗狀態符號 + 書籤 ⭐📌 | **無 format-string 插值** | **缺口**——原生 agent dots 取代 agent 部分 |
87:> **兩組 herdr 環境變數。** 上面那組 `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` **只**會被注入到 `[[keys.command]]` 的呼叫裡。而每個*跑在 herdr pane 內的 shell* 還會拿到一組**環境值 (ambient)**：`HERDR_ENV=1`、`HERDR_PANE_ID`、`HERDR_TAB_ID`、`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`、以及 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`（當前 session 的 socket）。腳本用 `HERDR_ENV` 當作「我在不在 herdr 裡？」的判斷，並繼承 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 來鎖定當前 session——這正是 `hvibe`/`hcode` 依賴的東西。
97:| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | 直接跳到 **agent** N 的 pane（`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
109:| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes`（即時 agent panes） | command pane |
110:| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts`（SSH picker） | command pane |
119:[`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) 裡有四個 shell 函式，就是 tmux 的 `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` 在 herdr 端的對應物。兩個**重量級**的（`hvibe` / `hcode`）能一氣呵成拉起整個 coding workspace；兩個**輕量級**的（`hhere` / `hroot`）只是在某個目錄開一個純 workspace 並 attach——不需要 git repo，也沒有 agent layout。它們呼叫原生的 `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI，並**原封不動重用純邏輯**（specstory 包裝、`--on-exit shell|kill|restart`、git-root 解析、agent-CLI 偵測），這些來自 `22_sesh.sh`；只有 layout 呼叫不同。需要 `herdr` server 正在跑 + `jq`。
131:- **Attach 感知（像 svibe 的 `$TMUX` 分支）**：從 herdr **內部**跑 → workspace/tab 的 focus 呼叫會切換活著的 client（不開新 client）。從 herdr **外部的一般終端**跑 → 輔助函式會拉起一個 attach 到該 session 的 client，讓新 workspace 真的看得到（herdr 的 `workspace focus` 只會移動*已經 attach* 的 client，所以少了這步，整包會被建在看不見的地方）。`--no-attach` 兩種情況都以 detach 方式建立。判斷依據是環境值 `HERDR_ENV`。
133:- **Agent 可見性**：herdr **逐 pane** 追蹤 agent 狀態，所以在預設的 splits layout 下，每個 agent 仍會在 herdr 的 agent 追蹤裡各自現身（已驗證：同一 tab 裡兩個 agent 會在 `herdr agent list` 顯示為兩筆）。緊湊的左側欄會把一個 *tab* 的狀態彙整成一個點——若你要每個 agent 各擁有一個 tab 層級的狀態點，用 `--tab-per-agent`。
137:tmux 的 `svibe` / `scode` 仍是 tmux 端的對應物（見 [sesh](sesh.md)）；兩個家族共存——`hvibe`/`hcode` 只碰 herdr，`svibe`/`scode` 只碰 tmux。
153:## Television 整合
155:大多數 `tv` channel（`tools`、`fleet-hosts`、`mlflow`、`kill-process`、`ssh-config`）的 action **不與 tmux 耦合**，所以在 herdr command pane 裡原樣就能跑——綁一個鍵到 `tv <channel>` 即可。只有那些 action 會呼叫 `tmux …` 的 channel 才需要 herdr-aware 變體。這裡出貨兩個：
158:- `herdr-agent-panes`（`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`）—— 與 `agent-panes` 同來源，但切換/kill 改用 `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`。
202:兩個原生層，不需要 plugin：
237:本 repo 的預設立場是 herdr **或** tmux,不巢狀。但你可以刻意巢狀——tmux 當外層視窗管理器,內含數個 herdr client,有些本地、有些 `herdr --remote <host>` 連到不同 server。癥結是 **prefix 衝突**:兩者都預設 `Ctrl+b`,所以外層 tmux 吃掉它,內層 herdr 永遠收不到自己的 prefix（[herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)）。
247:## AI 用量 / 額度狀態
249:herdr **沒有原生的用量/額度/token 顯示**（側欄只顯示 agent *狀態*）。它確實有一個逐 pane 的 hook——`herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N`——driver 可以把 `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` 之類的標籤推進去。有一個 Codex-only 的社群 plugin（[jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)）已從 [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) 讀的同一份 `~/.codex` 資料做到這件事；但沒有東西涵蓋 Claude/ChatGPT 額度。延後——CodexBar 的選單列仍是多供應商的檢視。設計與選項記在 [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md)。
255:- **狀態列 format 符號 + 書籤**（⭐/📌/🔖）：herdr 沒有 `#{@option}` 的 format-string 插值。原生 agent dots 涵蓋 agent 部分；手動書籤沒有對應物。
258:> **不是缺口：** vi copy-mode 本身*是*原生（`prefix+[`），且逐 pane 的 agent 狀態是原生偵測——我原本以為會缺的兩件事，結果都內建了。
262:- [tmux 設定](tmux/README.md) · [Television (tv)](tv.md) · [sesh](sesh.md) · [workmux](workmux.md)

255	
256	- **無縫 `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane 導覽。** `vim-tmux-navigator` 與 tmux 耦合（`is_vim` 的 `ps`/`pane_tty` 啟發式 + nvim plugin）。herdr 沒有 smart-splits 對應物——它的 pane focus 是 `prefix+h/j/k/l`，在邊界不會穿透進 nvim 的 splits。Workaround：在 nvim 裡用它自己的 `<C-w>hjkl`。這是相對 tmux 最大的 UX 退步。

260

1	# herdr usage-status driver — CodexBar-analog AI quota in the herdr sidebar
2	
3	**Status**: P? — researched, not spiked yet (deliberately deferred 2026-07)
4	**Effort**: M (DIY driver, Codex+Claude) / S (just install the Codex-only plugin)
5	**Related**: [docs/tools/herdr.md](../docs/tools/herdr.md), `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (`hvibe`/`hcode`), `dot_config/shell/40_codexbar` (existing CodexBar shell aliases `cbu`/`cbc`/`cbca`), [steipete/CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) (brew cask `codexbar`, already installed)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	herdr's sidebar shows per-pane agent **state** (idle / working / blocked) natively but has **no usage / quota / token display** — confirmed against `herdr --default-config` (v0.7.1): no `statusline` / `status_bar` / `usage` / `quota` / `widget` keys; `[ui]` only exposes `sidebar_*_width`. The user already runs **CodexBar** (macOS menu bar, multi-provider: Codex + Claude + ChatGPT + …) as the usage view, wired into the shell via `40_codexbar` (`cbu`/`cbc`/`cbca`). The question was whether the same "% used" info can live **inside herdr** next to the agents.
10	
11	Decision at research time: **keep CodexBar as the primary usage view; do not install a herdr plugin now.** Backlog a DIY driver for when the user lives in herdr full-time and wants Claude+Codex quota in the sidebar without alt-tabbing to the menu bar.
12	
13	## The hook (verified)
14	
15	herdr can render arbitrary status TEXT next to a pane/agent in the sidebar via the metadata API:
16	
17	```
18	herdr pane report-metadata <pane_id> --source <id> --custom-status "Claude 62% • Codex 78%5h" --ttl-ms <n>
19	```
20	
21	`--custom-status` + `--ttl-ms` (auto-expiry) is exactly the driver surface — a background timer computes the string and pushes it per pane. (`herdr pane report-agent … --custom-status` is the other entry point.) No core/config change required.
22	
23	## Prior art (herdr plugins)
24	
25	- **[jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)** — closest analog to CodexBar's *Codex* provider. Reads local Codex JSONL at `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` (default `~/.codex/sessions`), finds the newest `rate_limits` event, publishes a compact `"78%5h 64%wk"` label into the agents sidebar via a background service, plus a `codex-usage-watch` refreshing pane. **Same on-disk source CodexBar uses for Codex; no OpenAI API call.** Codex-ONLY.
26	- **[Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard](https://github.com/Davidcreador/herdr-token-dashboard)** — per-agent token/cost TUI pane (Pi session JSONL + OpenCode server API). Token/cost, not subscription quota.
27	- **Gap**: no herdr plugin covers **Claude / ChatGPT** subscription quota. CodexBar gets those from OAuth/cookies/CLI, which nothing in the herdr ecosystem mirrors.
28	
29	## Options when this is picked up
30

echo "=== pane get (custom_status set? agent_status intact?) ==="

echo "=== tv channel source query lists it? ==="

echo "=== toggle (should clear, since flagged) ==="; "$SCRIPT" toggle "$PANE"
echo "=== pane get after toggle (custom_status gone?) ==="
herdr pane get "$PANE" | jq -c '{agent_status:.result.pane.agent_status, custom_status:.result.pane.custom_status}'

Short answer: No — there’s no documented [menu] config or supported way to add arbitrary items to the built‑in right‑click pane/context menu.

Evidence and relevant notes:
- The docs show custom keybindings and custom commands (pane/shell/plugin_action): "Custom commands use the same keybinding syntax." 
- Custom commands can run things and get pane context via env vars: "Custom commands receive HERDR_SOCKET_PATH, HERDR_BIN_PATH, HERDR_ACTIVE_WORKSPACE_ID, HERDR_ACTIVE_TAB_ID, HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, and HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD when those values are available."
- The right‑click passthrough setting mentions Herdr’s pane menu but does not document menu contents or a menu config: "Set right_click_passthrough_modifier = \"ctrl\" ... reach the app instead of opening Herdr’s pane menu."

What this implies (from the doc text):
- You cannot declare extra right‑click menu items via a [menu] table in config — no such table or menu‑extension API is documented on the configuration page.
- You can add custom command keybindings that run commands (pane, shell, or plugin actions) and those commands can receive pane-context env vars when available.
- There is no documented mechanism to run a command specifically against "the pane/agent under the mouse cursor"; custom commands act with the focused pane’s context (the docs say shell commands "run from the focused pane’s working directory when Herdr can detect it"), and menu behavior is not exposed for extension.

If you want per‑pane/custom actions, use custom keybindings / plugin_action entries; the right‑click menu itself is not shown as user‑extensible in the provided docs.

查清楚了,直接回答。

## 不行 —— herdr 的右鍵選單不能自訂

herdr 的右鍵打開的是**固定的內建 pane menu**,官方 config **沒有 `[menu]` table、也沒有任何選單擴充 API**(這跟 tmux 完全不同 —— tmux 的 `display-menu` 是全可編程的,所以你那個 `MouseDown3Status` 書籤才做得出來)。

而且 herdr 的自訂命令(`[[keys.command]]`)**只能綁到鍵**,綁不到滑鼠鍵或選單項;它拿到的 pane context 是 `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`(**focus 中的** pane),也沒有「游標下那個 pane」的概念。所以「右鍵 agents 欄位那一列 → 標記」這條路在 herdr 走不通。

滑鼠在 herdr 能做的只有:點一下 focus、右鍵開內建選單(不可改)、滾輪。

## 可行的替代(由近到遠)

1. **點一下 + 鍵**:滑鼠點該 agent 列把它 focus 起來 → 按 `prefix+m`。這是最接近「滑鼠操作」的方式(click-to-focus 是原生的)。
2. **鍵盤直接**:`prefix+m` toggle(已做好)。
3. **選單式觸發**:herdr 唯一可擴充的「選單」是 herdr-plus 的 **Quick Actions**(`prefix+y`,你已裝)—— 那是個 fuzzy 命令選單,可加自訂項。我可以幫你在 Quick Actions 裡加「Mark / Unmark for review」兩項,這樣就有一個**選單入口**(雖然是 fuzzy 彈窗、不是右鍵)。

======================== #864 ========================
TITLE: [idea] "Mark unread" action for agents (re-flag a seen agent)
BY: yasinozmeen  UPVOTES: 3  COMMENTS: 0

--- BODY ---
### idea / problem

The agents panel already has the seen/unseen color logic — blue when unseen, green once I've looked at it. But there's no way to manually flip a green agent back to blue when I've only glanced at it and want to come back to it later.

### requested change

Add a Mark unread action to the agents right-click menu. One important detail: it should stick even for the agent I'm currently looking at. Today the active tab gets marked seen again on window focus and on agent activity, so a manual unread on the current agent wouldn't survive. So I'd treat a manual unread as sticky — automatic "seen" doesn't override it — and clear it only when I actually switch into that tab. (This builds on the agents right-click menu from my other idea, the Close one.)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0d96633-fc65-477e-83b8-2b3fa373b3fc



### why you want this

When I'm watching many agents, I often glance at one but want to deal with it later. Being able to re-flag it as unread keeps it visible instead of blending into the green "seen" ones. Working local build, all tests passing — happy to PR if you like the idea.

--- COMMENTS ---


======================== #906 ========================
TITLE: [idea] Plugin API: contribute items to the workspace / worktree sidebar context menu
BY: wyattjoh  UPVOTES: 2  COMMENTS: 2

--- BODY ---
### idea / problem

When I right-click a worktree entry in the sidebar I get a fixed, hard-coded menu: Rename, Close, Delete worktree checkout. There is no way for a plugin to add entries to that menu.

As a plugin author building worktree management tooling I need a contextual surface to offer actions like "Copy worktree path". The checkout path is already known to Herdr (it places it under `<worktrees.directory>/<repo>/<branch-slug>`) but there is no way to surface it to my clipboard today without leaving Herdr or asking users to memorise an arbitrary keybinding.

Keybindings are the only current plugin trigger surface, but they are not discoverable, and they do not carry the clicked workspace/worktree as implicit context. A right-click on the exact entry a user is looking at is the natural place to offer workspace-scoped plugin actions.

### requested change

Add a `[[context_menu_items]]` table to `herdr-plugin.toml` that lets plugins declare entries injected into the sidebar right-click menus for workspaces and worktrees.

Each item declares a label, which surface(s) it targets, and the action id to invoke. When the user clicks the item Herdr invokes the action exactly as it would for a keybinding-triggered action, and injects the same invocation context it already provides (`workspace id`, `worktree path`, `branch name`) as environment variables so the plugin command can act on what was right-clicked without any additional socket round-trips.

Minimal manifest sketch:

```
[[context_menu_items]]
id       = "copy-path"
label    = "Copy worktree path"
surfaces = ["worktree"]   # or ["workspace"], or both
action   = "copy-path"
```

The corresponding action entry stays unchanged. The plugin receives `HERDR_WORKTREE_PATH` (or equivalent) and can write to the clipboard via the OS, call back through `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, or do anything else a normal plugin action already can.

### why you want this

The immediate use case is a "Copy worktree path" menu item for a worktree management plugin. One click, path on the clipboard. No keybinding to remember, no pane to open.

But the same mechanism unlocks a whole class of contextual worktree actions: running post-checkout setup scripts on a freshly created worktree, offering a teardown flow that goes beyond "Delete worktree checkout", or opening the path in another tool. All of these are naturally right-click actions because the user is already looking at the worktree entry when they want to act on it.

Context menus are the right UX here because they are discoverable (users find them by right-clicking, not by reading docs), contextual (the clicked item is the implicit target), and composable (multiple installed plugins can each contribute entries without conflicting). Keybindings are a poor substitute for this pattern.

--- COMMENTS ---
@tdi: I am highly supporting this for plugins - use cases are for example running a reviewer on space / agent or creating new wt from a gh PR. 

@tdi: Quick technical feasibility pass against the current codebase: **yes, this is very doable**, and it composes cleanly off three things that already exist.

**1. Plugin action invocation already exists.** `invoke_plugin_action_from_keybind()` runs a declared `[[actions]]` entry with workspace context. A context-menu trigger is the same flow with a different `invocation_source`.

**2. The invocation context already carries the worktree.** `PluginInvocationContext` injects `workspace_id`, `workspace_cwd`, and the full `worktree` snapshot (including `checkout_path` + branch). So a "Copy worktree path" action already has everything it needs — no new context plumbing. (Today the path only ships in `HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON`; a dedicated `HERDR_WORKTREE_PATH` env var alongside `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` would be a one-line addition to match this proposal.)

**3. The right-click context menu already exists.** `ContextMenuKind` (Workspace / GitWorkspace / Tab / Pane), `Mode::ContextMenu`, `render_context_menu`, and dispatch via `MouseAction::ContextMenu { menu, idx }` are all in place. The right-click handler already knows the clicked `ws_idx`.

**What would actually have to change:**

- **Manifest**: a `[[context_menu_items]]` table (id, label, action) plus validation that each `action` references a declared action — this is the same validation pattern already used for `[[link_handlers]]`.
- **Menu items become dynamic**: today `ContextMenuState::items()` returns a hardcoded `&'static [&'static str]` and dispatch matches by string label. That needs to become a computed list (built-in labels + appended plugin labels + a separator) so render and dispatch share one list.
- **Dispatch branch**: clicks on plugin-item indices route to a new `invoke_plugin_action_from_context_menu(action_id, ws_idx)`.
- **One correctness detail worth calling out**: the existing keybind path builds context from the *active* workspace (`current_plugin_context`). For a context menu the context must come from the *clicked* entry — `plugin_context_for_workspace(ws_idx)` already exists for exactly this, so it's a straightforward swap, but it's the thing to get right.

**One design suggestion:** the proposed `surfaces = ["worktree", "workspace"]` field overlaps with the existing `contexts: Vec<PluginActionContext>` field on actions (`Global | Workspace | Tab | Pane | Selection`). Reusing `contexts` (where `Workspace` already covers both workspaces and worktree entries today) avoids two parallel gating mechanisms in the manifest.

No architectural changes, no runtime/client boundary concerns (menu = TUI presentation; action dispatch reuses the existing server invocation path). It's roughly one small refactor + six small additions, all following patterns already in the codebase.
```
</details></tool-use>
